newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion down on fresh supplies, world trend.
newsitem.headline: India bullion down on fresh supplies, world trend.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat opened 25 rupees lower at 4,430 rupees per 10 gramme on the back of fresh arrivals and losses in the world market.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) opened 300 rupees lower at 51,800 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Monday.
** Silver (.999) opened 55 rupees lower at 6,265 rupees per kg on higher supplies of the imported silver and weak trend in the world market.

Gold 24 carat opened 25 rupees lower at 4,430 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,455 rupees on the back of fresh arrivals while a setback in the world market prompted fresh selling, dealers said.
Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday after gaining 120 rupees last week.
"Demand resistance from the physical buyers also dragged prices lower," one dealer said.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.64 gramme) opened 300 rupees lower at 51,800 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Monday. They were up by 1,400 rupees last week.

Silver (.999) opened 55 rupees lower at 6,265 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,320 rupees on higher arrivals of imported silver while industrial buyers kept to the sidelines after the world market setback. Silver was down by 50 rupees per kg on Monday and by 90 rupees last week.
Arrivals of imported silver remained higher at 1,500/2,000 kgs in the Bombay market and sentiment was subdued in early trade.
